## 1. Come, let us call  (`#come-let-us-call`)

Cited ayat: 3:59-61

> **3:59** إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
>
> **3:60** ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ
>
> **3:61** فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ فَقُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ نَدْعُ أَبْنَآءَنَا وَأَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَكُمْ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَكُمْ ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (3:59): The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was.

**c2** (3:60): The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters.

**c3** (3:61): The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.

**c4** (3:61): Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars.

### One-minute summary

The verses say that the likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam [c1], and that the truth is from the Lord of the one addressed [c2]. They tell him what to say to anyone who argues with him: let each side call their sons, their women and themselves, and earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was [c1]. The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters [c2].

The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves [c3]. Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c4].

### Deep study

The passage begins with a likeness and ends with an invitation [c1][c3]. The pronoun in 'about him' is not resolved in the verse; it can be read as Isa or as the truth stated before it [c3]. The invitation names groups to be called, sons, women and ourselves, and leaves the persons unnamed [c3]. What follows the supplication is a curse upon the liars, and the verse says no more [c4].

### Kids mode

The verses say that God made Isa like He made Adam: from dust, then He said "Be", and he was [c1]. They say that the truth is from the Lord [c2]. They tell what to say to those who argue: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage meets an argument with an invitation to turn together to God [c3][c4]. Another is that it begins from a likeness, Isa and Adam, before it turns to the invitation [c1][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who argued, where, or when. The verse says 'anyone who argues with you about him'.
- Not established: whether the invitation was carried out, who came, or how it ended; the verses do not say.
- Not established: who 'our sons', 'our women' and 'ourselves' refer to.
- The pronoun in 'about him' (3:61) is read in more than one way; the draft does not decide.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the people who argued, the people called, the place and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.
